content: The guidelines, clauses, and limits for bacterial larvicides are similar to those outlined in Sections 4 to 8 of this manual. However, specific differences in requirements and objectives are detailed below. When Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti) formulations are proposed for use in drinking water, the specifications must include parameters for color, taste, and odor. The maximum acceptable levels of microbial contaminants for drinking water or other public health applications have not yet been determined. Product Description The active ingredient must be described by its bacterial genus, species, and strain. If the product is intended for use in drinking water, the description should also include details about its color, odor, and taste. Active Ingredient Identity The bacterial species and strain must be clearly identified, and the reference standard material must be traceable to an internationally recognized culture collection. Active Ingredient Content The content of the active ingredient must be clearly defined, and a method for assessing its biological potency (toxicity to target mosquito species) must be provided. Microbial Impurities The content of microbial contaminants must be limited to reduce risks associated with handling and to maintain the efficacy of the product. Microbial impurities can be introduced during sampling and may increase over time. Therefore, sampling and testing must be conducted in specialized facilities by trained personnel. Currently, the World Health Organization (WHO) determines acceptable levels on a case-by-case basis. Chemical Impurities The product must be free of beta-exotoxin, which could harm non-target organisms. This is verified using a fly larvae toxicity test or an equivalent high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) method. Storage Stability Storage stability is addressed on a case-by-case basis. For bacterial larvicide technical concentrates (TK), draft specifications must not omit or relax clauses without justification. Notes provided in the guidelines should only be incorporated if applicable to the specific product. Description of Technical Concentrates The material must consist of the specified bacterial genus, species, subspecies, and strain, along with by-products from the manufacturing process. It should be free from visible extraneous matter and added agents, except stabilizers or free-flow agents if required. Identity Testing The active ingredient must pass an identity test and, if necessary, additional tests to confirm its identity. Bioassay for Biological Potency The biological potency of Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis (Bti) and Bacillus sphaericus (Bsph) products is determined by comparing the mortality of mosquito larvae caused by the test product to that caused by a reference standard. Reference powders, such as IPS 82 for Bti and SPH 88 for Bsph, are used for calibration. The bioassay involves early fourth-instar larvae of Aedes aegypti (for Bti) or Culex pipiens pipiens (for Bsph). The toxicity of IPS 82 is set at 15,000 ITU/mg, while SPH 88 is set at 1,700 ITU/mg. Use of Alternative Reference Standards Alternative bacterial larvicide reference powders or mosquito strains must be carefully cross-calibrated against the recognized standards. Cross-calibration should ideally be conducted by independent expert laboratories, and the data must be made available for verification. Preparation of Reference Suspensions Reference suspensions for bioassays are prepared by mixing the reference powder with deionized water and a wetting agent. The suspension is homogenized, and any aggregates are removed. Aliquots of the suspension can be stored at 4°C for one month or frozen at -18°C for up to two years. Bioassay Procedure The bioassay involves exposing mosquito larvae to various concentrations of the test product and recording mortality rates at 24 and 48 hours. For Bti, the 24-hour count is used, while for Bsph, the 48-hour count is preferred due to its slower action. Tests with high control mortality (>5%) or excessive pupation (>5%) are invalid. Statistical programs, such as SAS, are recommended for analyzing dose-response data. Larvae Production Early fourth-instar larvae are used for testing, as they represent the target population's sensitivity. Storage Stability Testing Products must demonstrate no more than a 10% loss in biological potency when stored at 5°C for two years or at 20–25°C for one year. Representative product samples are tested using the bioassay method described earlier. Variations in bioassay results of up to ±25% are acceptable. Wettable Powders (WP) Wettable powders must consist of a homogeneous mixture of the specified bacterial strain, fillers, and other necessary formulants. The formulation should be dry, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter. The active ingredient content must meet the declared minimum potency, and the product must be free of beta-exotoxin. Notes on Testing Odor and taste may be important for products intended for drinking water applications, but no standardized tests exist for these characteristics. If tested, the product should be diluted to its highest use rate.
